\section[prevenir]{prevenir — to prevent, to head off; to warn}

\label{lesson:ES-C614-prevenir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for likely, then the Spanish for the probability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: prevenir}
\textbf{prevenir} — \textquotedblleft{}to prevent, to head off; to warn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es mejor prevenir los problemas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is better to prevent problems.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{venir}: \emph{prevengo, previne}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{prevenir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{praevenire} 'to come before, to anticipate', built from \emph{prae} and \emph{venire} 'to come' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prevenir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prevenir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{prevenir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for likely, then the Spanish for the probability, then say \emph{prevenir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does prevenir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To prevent, to head off; to warn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[arriesgar]{arriesgar — to risk}

\label{lesson:ES-C614-arriesgar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the probability, then the Spanish for to prevent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: arriesgar}
\textbf{arriesgar} — \textquotedblleft{}to risk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No quiero arriesgar mi dinero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not want to risk my money.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Arriesgarse} — to take a chance. Spelling: \emph{arriesgué}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{arriesgar} is built on \emph{riesgo} 'risk', which comes from Italian \emph{rischio} (EtymDB); the older origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arriesgar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arriesgar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{arriesgar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the probability, then the Spanish for to prevent, then say \emph{arriesgar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does arriesgar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To risk\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[garantizar]{garantizar — to guarantee}

\label{lesson:ES-C614-garantizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to prevent, then the Spanish for to risk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: garantizar}
\textbf{garantizar} — \textquotedblleft{}to guarantee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No te puedo garantizar nada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I cannot guarantee you anything.}
\end{quote}

Spelling: \emph{garanticé}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{garantizar} is built on \emph{garantía}; EtymDB links \emph{garantía} with Catalan \emph{garantia} and English \emph{guarantee}, and the family is usually traced to Old French \emph{garant} 'guarantor', from a Frankish word for a protector.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{garantizar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{garantizar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{garantizar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to prevent, then the Spanish for to risk, then say \emph{garantizar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does garantizar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To guarantee\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la garantía]{la garantía — the guarantee, the warranty}

\label{lesson:ES-C614-garantia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to risk, then the Spanish for to guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la garantía}
\textbf{la garantía} — \textquotedblleft{}the guarantee, the warranty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El móvil tiene dos años de garantía.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The phone has a two-year warranty.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar en garantía} — to be under warranty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{garantía} comes from \emph{garante} 'guarantor'; EtymDB links it with Catalan \emph{garantia}, and the family is usually traced to Old French \emph{garant}, from a Frankish word for a protector.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la protección]{la protección — the protection}

\label{lesson:ES-C614-proteccion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to guarantee, then the Spanish for the guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la protección}
\textbf{la protección} — \textquotedblleft{}the protection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Usa protección solar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Use sun protection.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Proteger} — to protect.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{protección} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{protectio} 'a covering over', built on \emph{protegere}, from \emph{tegere} 'to cover' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
